name: How do you prevent sewer odor in an ADU bathroom?

mainEntity.name: Why does an ADU bathroom sometimes smell like sewer gas and how can it be avoided?
mainEntity.text: Why does an ADU bathroom sometimes smell like sewer gas and how can it be avoided?

acceptedAnswer.text: Sewer odor in an ADU bathroom usually means something is wrong with the trap, venting, or drain connection. A dry P-trap, loose toilet seal, poor venting, or a poorly detailed pipe penetration can allow odors back into the room. In a new ADU bathroom, the best way to prevent this is to design the plumbing correctly from the start and test it before the walls are closed. The contractor should verify that every fixture has proper trapping, that venting is sized and routed correctly, and that all penetrations are sealed. If the ADU is used intermittently, unused drains can dry out over time, so periodic water use may be needed. Homeowners should also be careful not to ignore minor odors, because they can signal a bigger plumbing or venting issue. In a compact bathroom, even a small odor problem can make the entire unit feel unfinished or poorly built. Early correction is far cheaper than opening finished walls later.
acceptedAnswer.description: Sewer odor usually comes from dry traps, poor venting, loose seals, or an improper drain connection. In an ADU bathroom, the best prevention is correct vent design, properly trapped fixtures, airtight sealing at penetrations, and regular use of the shower and sinks. Odor problems should be fixed before finishes are closed up.
